Extra Text

Willem Hendrik van den Berg learnt the basics of painting from his father and went on to study at the Academie van Beeldende Kunsten in The Hague, where his tutors included Willem van Konijnenburg.

He painted figures and portraits, as well as animals - particularly birds - in a detailed and highly recognisable style. Around 1930, he produced various sketches of animals at Artis Zoo, a number of which are held in the archives of the Rijksacademie in Amsterdam. He was a member of Arti in Amsterdam, Pulchri Studio in The Hague, and the Gooise Painters’ Association in Laren.

The family originally came from The Hague and moved to Amsterdam around 1938/39 when Willem became a professor at the Rijksacademie. They first lived on Churchillaan, then in Lekstraat. Towards the end of his life, the painter lived on Zomerdijkstraat in Amsterdam, in a small house with a studio.

Through his granddaughter, a number of family portraits and some works by his father, Andries, are being offered in this auction.

This lot is accompanied by 2 works on paper by Andries van den Berg (1852-1944): 
I. Two praying women in Bruges, watercolour on paper, 17x14 cm (full sheet: 28x22,5 cm), dated and signed with monogram '1925/AB' (lower right).
II. Chickens and a woman in a barn in South Limburg, watercolour on paper, 23,5x33,5 cm,annotated and signed 'Zuid Limburg/A van den Berg/Voor: Hekker' (on the reverse).

Andries van den Berg (The Hague, 1852 -1944) studied at the Academie van Beeldende Kunsten in The Hague under Johan Philip Koelman. He was a member of Arti et Amicitiae, and from 1878 to 1918 he was a drawing teacher at the Haagse Academie. His pupils included, alongside his son Willem Hendrik van den Berg, Mijndert van den Berg, Cornelis Koppenol, Gerbrand Frederik van Schagen, Leendert van der Vlist and Jan Wittenberg.
Initially, he worked in a romantic style, but around 1900 he developed a more impressionist style, with subjects drawn from everyday life.

Extra Text

Petrus Camper (Leiden 1722-The Hague 1789), was a Dutch physician, anatomist, physiologist, midwife, zoologist, anthropologist, palaeontologist and a naturalist in the Age of Enlightenment. In 1763 he accepted the chair of anatomy, surgery and botany at the University of Groningen. He made drawings to illustrate his eloquent lectures. His main focus of attention was anatomy, zoology and his collection of minerals and fossils.

In 1774, a young male elephant died at the stadtholder’s menagerie near The Hague. Camper was permitted to dissect the carcass; he had completed the dissection within three weeks and produced a large number of drawings. His research yielded various new findings, including details on the skeleton of the legs, the structure of the skull and brain, and the muscles and nerves of the trunk. Camper’s drawings are held, amongst other places, in the collection of the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

Extra Text

This is a counterproof (contre-épreuve) of a copy made by Karel la Fargue after a drawing by Jan van Goyen  (1596-1656) (sold at: Auction, Sotheby Mak van Waay, Amsterdam, 15 November 1983, lot 245; Beck 1972/73, vol. I, 1972, p. 48, no. 141). 

La Fargue first produced a forged copy after a drawing by Jan van Goyen and subsequently created this counterproof (contre-épreuve), resulting in a reversed image. As was customary in his working method, the transferred impression was reinforced and reworked in black chalk to restore weakened contours and to imitate the appearance of an original seventeenth-century drawing. This drawing is therefore a counterproof of a forgery that itself was copied from a drawing by Jan van Goyen. La Fargue later produced a further counterproof from the present sheet, continuing the sequence of replicas derived from the same composition. Notably, in this first counterproof he omitted the inn sign that appears in the source composition. The drawing forms part of a documented series of counterproofs and reworked replicas associated with La Fargue’s extensive practice of imitating and forging seventeenth-century Dutch landscape drawings.

To date, 235 forged drawings after seventeenth-century Dutch masters by Karel la Fargue are known; for a general discussion, see Charles Dumas and Michiel Plomp, ‘Karel la Fargue (1738-1793) as a forger of seventeenth-century Dutch drawings’, in Oud Holland 1998, p. 1-23. Of these, at least 29 are forgeries after drawings by Jan van Goyen.

Extra Text

Chin A Foeng was born in Paramaribo and displayed a remarkable talent for drawing from an early age. In order to further develop his skills, he attended classes at the CCS-School voor Beeldende Kunsten (School of Visual Arts) in Paramaribo, where he was taught, among others, by Nola Hatterman. As a teenager, he won several national and international drawing competitions, and at the age of 16 or 17 he was awarded a scholarship to pursue an art education in the Netherlands at the Academie van Beeldende Kunsten  in Tilburg. 

He subsequently continued his studies at the Rietveld Academie in Amsterdam, after which he returned to Suriname. There, he became an important advocate for art and cultural education and was involved in the establishment of several educational institutions. In the 1970s, he travelled to New York to pursue a master’s degree at New York University. Upon his return to Suriname, he devoted himself to establishing a fully-fledged art academy in Paramaribo, an ambition he succeeded in realizing in 1981. Sadly, Chin A Foeng died not long afterwards, at the age of just 39.

Relatively few works by Chin A Foeng are currently available on the market, making it difficult to find comparable works. The painting offered in the present auction bears a resemblance to the drawing ‘My House’, which he created at the age of 15 and submitted to a drawing competition in India (see: www.jules-chin.com/jaren-60).

The fact that the present work dates from circa 1960 makes it an early work, created before his formal art studies, at a stage when his artistic development was still in its formative years.

Extra Text

The Chinese/Indonesian artist Lee Man Fong (1913-1988) was known for his unique style, which combined traditional Chinese ink techniques with Western painting. Thanks to a scholarship, he spent a short period in the Netherlands between circa 1949 and 1952. Although he is best known for his oil paintings on board depicting animals and Balinese scenes, during this time in the Netherlands he captured typical Amsterdam characters with a blend of Eastern refinement and Western observation. This is evident in this etching of a ‘Herring Eater’: through his mastery of printmaking techniques, he demonstrates in this work his ability to capture everyday Dutch traditions with humour and attention to detail.

Soth 1998: Hammer price: € 9,916
Dit schilderij is wel al bij Vendu in Rotterdam op de veiling aangeboden en onverkocht gebleven (november 2023 en mei 2024). Zij hebben toen ook ontdekt dat de oorspronkelijke schilder niet juist was (Jean-Pierre Norblin de la Gourdaine).
